purpose: Figma component architecture. Source specification (hand-maintained). The Markdown component docs and the preview data are generated from this file; every variable named here must exist in Figma Variables (checked by validate-figma-variables.ps1).
iconNote: One Icon component set (24px, stroke from icon/stroke) with one variant per icon; the Icon instance-swap property points at it. The web system has 24 icons in 05-Assets/Icons.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Primary, secondary and text actions. The one component that carries most interactions.

properties.name: Size
properties.note: Sm and Lg exist in the web system

properties.name: Icon
properties.note: Swaps the icon shown in either slot

layout.widthSizing: HUG (set to FILL on phones for primary actions)
layout.padding: {control/padding-x/*} left and right, 0 top and bottom

components.variantNote: 3 x 3 x 5 = 45 variants. The state axis is a variant property (not a boolean) because each state changes fills and strokes.
components.responsive: Width is Hug on tablet and desktop; on phones the primary action is usually Fill container (the web has .btn--block-mobile). Height does not change by tier.
components.accessibility: Visual height 40, 48 or 56px; the 40px Sm button must keep a 44px hit area (place a transparent 44px frame behind it or add padding in the layout). Focus state shows a 2px ring with a 2px offset in color/focus/ring (color/focus/ring-inverse on the Inverse mode). The disabled label uses color/button/disabled-text on color/button/disabled-bg; disabled controls are exempt from contrast rules but stay legible.
components.handoff: Maps to .btn with .btn--primary, .btn--secondary or .btn--text and .btn--sm or .btn--lg. Use aria-disabled rather than disabled when focus must stay (loading). The web has no button loading state yet (open finding); do not design one here without approval.
notRepresentedInFigma: aria-busy and loading (not designed in the web system)

components.name: Icon Button
components.summary: Icon-only actions (search, account, bag, wishlist, close).

properties.name: Selected
properties.note: Pressed toggle, for example the wishlist heart (filled icon)

components.accessibility: Always needs an accessible name; Figma cannot enforce it, so the "Accessible name" text property exists to carry it into the handoff.
components.handoff: Maps to .icon-btn with aria-label and aria-pressed for toggles.

components.name: Input Field
components.summary: Label, control, hint and message for text, select and textarea.

properties.name: Required
properties.note: Adds the required marker to the label

layout.padding: {input/padding-x} left and right, {input/padding-y} top and bottom inside the control

components.responsive: Fill width; two fields may sit side by side from the Tablet mode (the web uses .grid--2 from 600px).
components.accessibility: The value text style is 16px (Form/Input) so iOS does not zoom on focus. An error is shown by a thicker error-coloured border plus an icon plus text, never colour alone. Control borders use color/control/border (3:1 or more on ivory and white); do not place a control directly on color/bg/subtle (2.8:1).
components.handoff: Maps to .field with .input, .select or .textarea; errors link through aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

components.name: Choice
components.summary: Checkbox and radio with a visible label.

properties.name: Checked
properties.note: A variant (not a boolean) because it changes the box fill, stroke and mark

layout.padding: vertical padding so the whole row is a 44px target

components.responsive: Same at every size; the row fills its container.
components.accessibility: The 24px box sits inside a row that is at least 44px high, so the whole row is the target. Checked state is a fill change plus a mark (shape), not colour alone.
components.handoff: Maps to .choice with a native input; groups use fieldset and legend (not representable in Figma: add a Group Label text layer and note it).
notRepresentedInFigma: indeterminate state (not in the web system)

components.name: Chip
components.summary: Filter toggle and removable applied-filter pill.

properties.name: Selected
properties.note: Selected adds a check mark (shape) as well as a tint

properties.name: Removable
properties.note: Shows the close icon (applied filters) and hides the check mark

components.responsive: On phones the choice row is a single horizontally scrolling line of chips (approved web decision 2): build it as an Auto Layout row with clipping on and padding above and below so the focus ring is not cut. From Tablet it wraps. Applied filters always wrap.
components.accessibility: Visual height 40px with a 44px hit area (add a transparent 44px frame). Selected is a tint plus a check mark plus a 2px border. A chip cut off at the row edge signals that the row scrolls.
components.handoff: Maps to .chip with aria-pressed; the scrolling row is .chip-row with chip-row.js, which keeps a focused chip fully visible.
notRepresentedInFigma: horizontal scrolling and scroll-into-view on focus (prototype with a scrolling frame to show intent)

components.name: Swatch
components.summary: Shade and colour chooser; the colour is product data.

properties.name: Size
properties.note: Sm is the decorative mini swatch on cards (not interactive)

properties.name: Selected
properties.note: Selected draws a 2px ring with an offset

properties.name: Shade name
properties.note: Displayed next to the group, not inside the swatch

components.variantNote: 2 x 2 x 3 = 12 variants. The swatch fill is a per-instance override of product data, deliberately NOT a variable (as in the web system, where it is an inline --swatch property).
components.accessibility: The selection ring (not the swatch colour) carries the 3:1 requirement, and the selected shade name is displayed as text.
components.handoff: Maps to .swatch with --swatch set inline from product data.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Short status or promotional label (Sale, New, Sold out, status tones).
components.responsive: Same at every size. On a 129 to 136px product card the Sale badge wraps onto two lines so it never runs under the wishlist button (web fix); keep Hug width and allow the label to wrap.
components.accessibility: A badge is text, so each tone must keep 4.5:1 between its text and fill (the status text colours are measured on their own tints at 5.3:1 or more).

components.name: Message
components.summary: Inline feedback with an icon and text (error, success, warning).

properties.name: Text
properties.default: Could not load more products. Check your connection and try again.

properties.name: Show action
properties.note: Optional action slot, for example Try again

components.accessibility: Never colour alone: icon plus text. Errors announce as alerts in the web implementation (role="alert").

components.name: Quantity Selector
components.accessibility: Each button is 44px; the value is a labelled number input.

components.name: Rating

properties.name: Value
properties.note: Filled stars (half stars are not in the web system)

components.accessibility: The stars are one image in the web implementation, named like "Rated 4 out of 5"; the filled and empty stars also differ by fill shape, not only colour.
components.handoff: Maps to .rating with a role="img" label.

components.name: Accordion Item
components.summary: A disclosure row; several can be open at once (approved web decision 3).

layout.padding: summary row at least {touch-target/min} high; panel padding {space/5} bottom

components.variantNote: 2 x 3 = 6 variants. Rows are independent; there is no exclusive group in Figma either.
components.responsive: Fill width; the panel is capped at the reading measure.
components.accessibility: The whole summary row is the target (44px or more). Open and closed are shown by the chevron and the content, not colour.
components.handoff: Maps to native details and summary. Do not add a name attribute (exclusive behaviour) unless a documented use case needs it.

components.name: Breadcrumb

properties.name: Layout
properties.note: Compact is the phone pattern: parent plus current page on one line, the current page truncated (approved web decision 1)

properties.name: Items
properties.default: Home / Skincare / Serums / Rosewater Barrier Serum
properties.note: Documentation of the trail; build real items from Breadcrumb Item instances

components.variantNote: 2 variants. Place Breadcrumb in the Mobile mode frame with Layout = Compact, in Tablet and Desktop with Layout = Full.
components.responsive: Compact below the Tablet tier, Full from Tablet. Compact hides the ancestors above the parent (they are also absent from the accessibility tree on phones: an open point for screen-reader testing).
components.accessibility: Each link keeps a 44px target. The current page is plain text, not a link style.
components.handoff: Maps to nav.breadcrumb with an ordered list; the phone behaviour is CSS only in the web system.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Numbered pagination (tablet and desktop) and Load more (phones). PROVISIONAL: nothing is verified against Shopify.

properties.name: Pattern
properties.note: Load more is the phone pattern; Numbered the tablet and desktop pattern

properties.name: Load more state
properties.note: Only used when Pattern = Load more

properties.name: Status text
properties.note: Announced politely in the web implementation

layout.gap: {space/1} between page links; {space/3} in Load more

components.variantNote: 2 patterns; Load more has 4 states (Load more reuses Button and Message instances). 2 + 4 = 6 variants, not 8: Numbered has no loading states.
components.responsive: Load more on Mobile frames, Numbered from Tablet. A phone in landscape (600px or wider) gets the Numbered pattern.
components.accessibility: Page links keep 44px targets; the current page is a fill plus bold text, not colour alone. Loading is announced and focus stays on the button in the web implementation.
components.handoff: Maps to .pagination-switch (CSS shows one pattern), .load-more and load-more.js. Real URLs (?page=N) must stay as links. Recovery from a mid-list URL (Load previous) is NOT designed because it is undecided (web foundations.md section 14, risk A).
notRepresentedInFigma: URL synchronisation, reload, shared links, back and forward, scroll restoration (all unverified in the web system)
focus moving to the first new item
components.statusNote: Load more on phones is provisional: nothing is verified against Shopify and no Load previous recovery is designed.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: Filter and sort panel: a full-width sheet on phones, a 416px side panel from tablet (approved web decision 5).

properties.name: Presentation
properties.note: Sheet = Mobile; Panel = Tablet and Desktop

properties.name: Show scrim
properties.note: Scrim beside the Panel (the Sheet covers the viewport)

layout.widthSizing: Sheet: FILL the viewport; Panel: FIXED {layout/drawer-width}
layout.gap: 0 (head, body and footer are separate regions; only the body scrolls)

components.variantNote: 2 variants. Contains instances of Icon Button, Button and Choice.
components.responsive: Sheet in the Mobile mode, Panel in Tablet and Desktop. The Layout collection variable layout/drawer-width is reference-only on Mobile (the sheet fills the screen).
components.accessibility: A close button (44px) and a pinned primary action are always visible. In the web implementation the drawer is a modal dialog with a focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus restore; Figma shows none of that, so document it on the component and test it in a browser.
components.handoff: Maps to dialog.drawer with drawer.js. aria-labelledby points at the title.
notRepresentedInFigma: focus trap, Escape, background scroll lock, focus restore (implemented and tested in Chromium only; manual tests pending)

components.name: Product Card
components.summary: Collection and search result card: image, badges, wishlist, brand, title, rating, price, swatches, quick action.

properties.name: State
properties.note: Hover zooms the image slightly on pointer devices only

properties.name: Sold out
properties.note: Muted image plus a Sold out badge; the action becomes disabled

properties.name: Image
properties.note: The 4:5 canvas is the PROVISIONAL default (no real photography yet)

components.variantNote: 3 variants plus booleans for optional parts. No combinatorial explosion: optionality is booleans, not variants.
components.responsive: Placed in a 2, 3 or 4 column grid from the Layout modes (gutter and gap follow the mode). A phone card is 129 to 136px wide at 320px (171px at 390px): the badge area reserves room for the 44px wishlist button and the badge label wraps.
components.accessibility: One link target (the title); the whole card shows the focus ring where the browser supports :has(), otherwise the title link shows it. Do not place text directly on photography without a solid panel or scrim.
components.handoff: Maps to .product-card; the image is a .ratio frame (4:5 provisional). Hover zoom is a prototype interaction only.
notRepresentedInFigma: real photography (none supplied): crop, focal point and packaging visibility are awaiting representative assets
components.statusNote: The 4:5 image canvas is a provisional default: no real photography has been supplied.

patterns.name: Filter row
patterns.note: Choice chips scroll horizontally on Mobile and wrap from Tablet; applied-filter chips always wrap.

patterns.name: Product grid
patterns.note: 2, 3 or 4 columns from the Layout modes; Load more on Mobile, Numbered from Tablet.

patterns.name: Filter drawer
patterns.note: Sheet on Mobile, Panel from Tablet; the footer action shows the result count.

notComponents: Header, navigation, mobile menu, footer (page sections, not in the web system yet)
Toast and cart drawer content (deferred in the web system)
Tabs, search with suggestions, skeleton loaders (not needed or Shopify features)

provisionalDecisions.title: Load more on phones (web decision 4)
provisionalDecisions.reason: No Shopify theme exists. The default fetch loader, URL synchronisation, reload, shared links, back and forward, scroll restoration and a Load previous (or equivalent) recovery are unverified or undecided.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: A Shopify theme with a collection of more than three pages, tested in Chrome, Safari and Firefox on a real phone; an owner decision on the recovery mechanism.

provisionalDecisions.title: 4:5 product image canvas (web decision 6)
provisionalDecisions.reason: No real product photography has been supplied. Crop, focal point, packaging visibility, responsive fit and loading are unvalidated.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Representative product assets (tallest and widest packaging, a white-background product, a lifestyle and a hero image) reviewed in the card, gallery and thumbnail at 320 to 1280px with real srcset delivery.

provisionalDecisions.title: Fluid sizes sampled in three modes
provisionalDecisions.reason: Figma cannot interpolate. The nine fluid web font sizes and the section spacing are held as three sampled values and can differ from the web between the sample widths (up to 8.6px for Display, 13px for section spacing).
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: An owner decision on whether the approximation is acceptable.

provisionalDecisions.title: Nothing has been created in Figma
provisionalDecisions.reason: No target file was approved, and the only connected account is a Dev seat with a guest role on a shared company team.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Approval of an empty new Figma design file where you can edit.

provisionalDecisions.title: Variables bound to Text Style properties
provisionalDecisions.reason: The specification binds font family, weight and size to variables inside Text Styles. This has not been tried in Figma.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Create one Text Style in the new file and read the bindings back.

provisionalDecisions.title: Font weight numbers to Figma style names
provisionalDecisions.reason: Weights are numbers (400, 500, 600, 700); Figma applies style names (Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold) that depend on the installed font.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Install the fonts in Figma and compare the style names.

provisionalDecisions.title: Opacity variable unit
provisionalDecisions.reason: Opacity is stored as a fraction (0 to 1) like the web; Figma may present 0 to 100.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Create one opacity variable and bind it to a layer.

provisionalDecisions.title: Plan limit on modes per collection
provisionalDecisions.reason: The proposal needs up to three modes in a collection; the limit on the account plan was not checked.
provisionalDecisions.evidenceNeeded: Check the plan, or create the collections in a new file.

pendingItems.note: The web system has no site-wide dark mode; none is invented.
